parameters.content:
## One Twilio sandbox number, two case studies
The Twilio WhatsApp sandbox allows exactly ONE inbound webhook URL, and Case 1 (real estate),
Case 2 (abandoned cart) and Case 3 (clinic appointments) share the account. Twilio points here; this
workflow decides which system owns the conversation and forwards the message unchanged.

**Case 1 is not modified in any way.** It still listens on `/whatsapp-inbound`, and if this router
is removed the only thing needed to restore the old behaviour is repointing the Twilio URL back.

Forwards go to `http://localhost:5678/...` - n8n calling itself INSIDE the container. Deliberately
not through the public tunnel: the tunnel is the least reliable component in this stack (four dead
hostnames so far), and a router that depends on it would drop replies whenever it flaps.

In a real deployment each client has their own WhatsApp sender and this workflow does not exist.

nodes.name: Note - Which system owns the phone

parameters.content:
## Which system owns the phone
Three systems now share one Twilio sandbox number.

| Most recent contact | Routed to | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Case 3 appointment `scheduled` / `reminded_*` / `confirmed`, or within 24h after the slot | Case 3 | live appointment - a confirmed patient still cancels, and "sorry I missed it" arrives late |
| Case 3 appointment `opted_out` | Case 3 | a repeat STOP is swallowed by the system that suppressed them |
| Case 3 waitlist entry `offered` | Case 3 | they are answering an offer we made |
| Cart pending_verification / abandoned / recovering / exhausted / opted_out | Case 2 | live or suppressed cart conversation |
| Cart recovered / converted_before_first_touch | Case 1 | the cart is closed, they bought |
| Nothing at all | Case 1 | unchanged behaviour |

**Case 3 wins a collision** and `multi_case_claim: true` is logged when both want the phone. An
unprocessed cancel costs a chair that cannot be resold; a misrouted cart reply costs one recovery
attempt. Not comparable.

**Lookup failure still fails OPEN toward Case 1** - the behaviour from before this workflow existed,
so an outage degrades instead of dropping the message. Logged as `router_lookup_failed`.

parameters.content:
## ⚠ إلغاء means opposite things in Case 2 and Case 3
Case 2 reads `إلغاء` as an **opt-out** — stop messaging me.
Case 3 reads `إلغاء` as **cancel my appointment** — and keeps sending reminders for anything else.

Nothing here reconciles them, and nothing needs to: this router hands each message to exactly ONE
system, so one message only ever gets one interpretation. That makes the routing decision above the
thing that determines which meaning applies.

Case 3's opt-out words are `توقف` / `STOP` / `UNSUBSCRIBE` / `ARRET` only.

Added 2026-08-09 with the Case 3 branch (Case 3 M3.1).
